name: Donepezil

lead: Donepezil is a prescription medicine for Alzheimer's dementia that increases acetylcholine in the brain. Some forum members ask about it as a nootropic.
Trials in dementia show modest cognitive benefits; its link to appearance is indirect, via cognitive performance.

paras: It reversibly blocks acetylcholinesterase, so acetylcholine lasts longer at synapses.
Nausea, diarrhea, insomnia, cramps and weight loss are common; the label warns of slow heart rate, heart block and GI bleeding. Prescription only.

forums.title: Where can I get Donepezil for my brain?

chain: Higher cholinergic signalling in the brain
Claimed sharper memory and focus for study, work and routine
angle.text: Some forum members discuss donepezil as a memory and focus aid. Its role in appearance is indirect, through whatever cognitive performance supports the rest of someone's looksmaxxing routine.

lead: Donepezil is a prescription cholinesterase inhibitor approved for dementia of the Alzheimer's type. By raising acetylcholine levels in the brain it is used to support memory and thinking. In looksmaxxing forums it comes up as a nootropic that some members ask about for focus and mental performance, an indirect route to ascending through better study, work and training consistency.[1][2][3]

It reversibly inhibits acetylcholinesterase, the enzyme that breaks down acetylcholine. The US label states there is no evidence it alters the course of the underlying dementia.[1] Trials and reviews report modest cognitive benefits in Alzheimer's disease, and it has also been studied in Lewy body dementia and other conditions.[4][5][6]

Common adverse reactions are nausea, diarrhea, insomnia, vomiting, muscle cramps, fatigue and anorexia, and the label warns of slowed heart rate and heart block, among other precautions.[3] It is available by prescription; one looksmax.org thread title shows members asking where to obtain it.[7]
infobox: Oral tablet, orally disintegrating tablet, transdermal patch

paras: The labelled use is symptomatic treatment of dementia of the Alzheimer's type at mild, moderate and severe stages.[3] Clinicians also prescribe it off-label for conditions such as dementia with Lewy bodies.[5][1]

A 24-week placebo-controlled trial of donepezil in Alzheimer's disease was published in 1998 by the Donepezil Study Group.[8] A 2012 trial examined donepezil continuation and memantine addition in moderate to severe disease,[9] and a 2004 trial tested memantine added to ongoing donepezil.[10]

A 2024 meta-analysis found improved cognition across Alzheimer's drugs including cholinesterase inhibitors,[2] while a 2021 review described the benefit of the class as mild.[4] A 2015 meta-analysis reported benefits of donepezil and rivastigmine for cognitive and psychiatric symptoms in Lewy body dementia.[5]
Researchers have also studied donepezil in healthy volunteers' attention[11] and in cognitive impairment after breast cancer chemotherapy.[12]

The label lists nausea, diarrhea, insomnia, vomiting, muscle cramps, fatigue and anorexia as most common, and warns about bradycardia, heart block, GI bleeding risk and exaggerated succinylcholine muscle relaxation during anesthesia.[3]
Pregnancy data in humans are inadequate.[3]
Donepezil reversibly inhibits acetylcholinesterase, increasing acetylcholine at synapses.[3] It is reported to be metabolised by CYP2D6 and CYP3A4.[1]
The FDA first approved donepezil in 1996, and approval was extended to severe Alzheimer's disease in 2006; a transdermal patch followed in 2022.[1]

lore.intro: Donepezil is rarely discussed on looksmaxxing forums, where it appears in nootropic-style questions about getting the drug for cognitive enhancement.[7]

claims.claim: Donepezil can boost memory and focus in healthy people

timeline.event: First US approval for mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease.[1]
